# Lease end of a never-connected vessel destroys a retained item's pane

Leaf of #18303 (parent linked natively). Promoted from #18621 item 3 — the never-rendered-vessel sighting, now a claim with its receipt. `Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029`.

> Corrected 2026-09-12 21:45Z, before any code: the first body said the dead window's binding was released and the host's retention answer "computed and discarded". A third run with a recorder on the host's `onNativeWindowRelease` showed it never ran — a vessel that never binds has no binding to release, and its lease runs from the reservation. The claim and the destroyer's stack are unchanged; the repair moved from "remember the answer" to "ask it once".

## Context

A tear-out vessel window can die before it ever connects: a popup blocked or closed within the first ~200 ms, before its app registers. The Workstation keeps such a vessel's workspace headless — the item stays in the vessel's own document, the participant stays registered (`committed: true`), and the topology bar offers `Open … as window` / `Show … here` (#18596, #18622). Twenty seconds after the tear-out the reconnect lease of the vessel's reservation runs out and the engine destroys the live pane, while every other owner still believes the item exists.

Measured at `dev@7e8b32e421` (headed Chromium, Neural Link reads only, the destroyer's own call stack recorded): three arms — the popup closed at the `popup` event with `page.close()` (twice) and with `page.close({runBeforeUnload: true})` — identical result. Receipt: the #18621 isolation comments and the rig in that ticket's session scratchpad (`IsolationLeaseEnd18621.scratch.spec.mjs`).

## The Problem

| when | fact |
|---|---|
| 0 | the tear-out reserves the vessel's slot; the 20 s reconnect lease starts at the reservation (`Transaction#reserve` → `startLease`, `Transaction.mjs:854`) |
| +111…151 ms | the popup is closed before its app binds: the slot still reads `{generation: 0, windowId: null}`, `findByWindow` has nothing for it, no `release` fires, and the Workstation's `onNativeWindowRelease` is never called (recorder silent for 32 s) |
| ≈ 20.1 s after the tear-out | `settleDockPane(neo-grid-container-2)` — the live pane is destroyed |
| same tick | `onDockPaneReturn({phase: 'after', returned: false})`, then `afterTearOutWindowDisconnect({itemId: 'feed', recovered: true, committed: true, expired: true})`; the vessel document still lists `feed`; `getPopupStates()` still reports the vessel `committed: true` with its host alive |

The destroy's stack, identical in all three arms:

```
settleDockPane                   src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:598          (the settlePane seam)
Object.reintegrateItem           src/dashboard/dock/window/TearOut.mjs:499
Object.onBindingReleased         src/dashboard/dock/window/TearOut.mjs:608
Object.expired                   src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:789
NativeLifecycle.onLeaseExpired   src/manager/transaction/NativeLifecycle.mjs:340
```

`reintegrateItem` reads the ROOT's committed document and finds no `feed` in it — the Workstation moved the item into `workstation-vessel:feed`'s document at the tear-out terminal — so it takes the no-home branch and settles the pane it was handed (`TearOut.mjs:496–500`). That pane is the one `capturePane` stored at the terminal (`dock/Workspace.mjs:976`, `TearOut.mjs:249–256`) and nothing released, because a vessel that never connects never adopts.

**The control — a vessel closed after it rendered, same rig, same held handle** (`heldPaneIds()` = `['feed']` before the close in every arm): the binding releases at +29 ms, `onNativeWindowRelease` answers `false`, the pane parks in the dead window's container, and nothing destroys it — no `settleDockPane`, no `afterTearOutWindowDisconnect` — for the full 32 s. Same handle, different route.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.manager.transaction.NativeLifecycle#onRelease` (`:302–325`) asks the source `unbind(data)` first and, when the answer is `false` (**retained**), skips the `released` effect: "Unbinds projection; false retains semantic ownership" / "Handles a released resource which was not retained" (`:62–63`). The dock Workspace supplies `unbind` from its `onNativeWindowRelease` hook (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:783`, `:805–809`); the Workstation answers `false` whenever the vessel's headless host exists (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:2578–2596`).
- A never-bound reservation has no binding, so `Transaction#release` finds nothing and `onRelease` never runs for it. `#onLeaseExpired` (`:333–341`) matches the never-connected admission (`!entry.connected`), calls `retire()` and fires the `expired` effect — the one route on which the host is never asked whether it retains the vessel. The route was written for "acknowledged cleanup of a provisional resource" (`:64`); a vessel whose document was committed and whose participant is registered is not provisional to its host.
- The dock Workspace's `expired` effect (`:788–790`) hands the context to `TearOut#onBindingReleased` with `committed: !!entry`; for a committed owner that means `releasePane` + `reintegrateItem` (`TearOut.mjs:603–612`) — the return-home flow of a single-document host, which on a multi-document host destroys the pane.
- `Workstation.view.Workspace#afterTearOutWindowDisconnect({itemId, recovered=true})` (`:2604–2614`) documents `recovered: false` — "when the vessel's workspace stays registered headless" — and nothing in the engine writes it: one reader, no writer, since #18309.
- Recovery from the destroyed state rebuilds the pane: `resolvePane` sees `isDestroyed` and creates again (`:1801–1808`), so the vessel lifecycle's same-live-instance contract fails silently on this route.

## The Fix

Ask the host the question the release route asks, on the one route that never did — and give the documented `recovered: false` its writer.

1. `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, the `expired` effect (`:788–790`): before handing the context to `onBindingReleased`, call `me.onNativeWindowRelease({groupId, workspaceKey, windowId: null, expired: true})` — the same hook `unbind` routes to, with the slot the lease freed and no window, since none ever bound. On `false` (retained): skip `onBindingReleased` — no `releasePane`, no `reintegrateItem`, no settle — and call `afterTearOutWindowDisconnect({...context, committed: !!entry, expired: true, recovered: false, pane: null})`, so the host runs its park-geometry and park-handler cleanup without retiring the retained target. Otherwise unchanged.
2. Docblocks: `onNativeWindowRelease` gains the expiry call in its contract (`windowId: null`, `expired: true`); `afterTearOutWindowDisconnect` documents `recovered` and `expired`.
3. No change to `NativeLifecycle`, `TearOut.mjs` or the Workstation, whose hook has read `recovered` since #18309.

Alternative weighed: a new lifecycle effect, or a `retained` flag computed by `NativeLifecycle` and carried in the `expired` payload. Both move the host's retention question into the manager, which owns no projection and would have to ask the source anyway; the host already answers it for the release route, and asking there keeps one answerer.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback / Edge Case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace#onNativeWindowRelease(data)` (`:805–809`) | this leaf; #18314 (the release route that already calls it) | also called by the host's own `expired` effect, once, with `{groupId, workspaceKey, windowId: null, expired: true}` when a never-bound reservation's lease ends; `false` retains | hosts that do not override it answer `true` and take the existing reintegration path (the dock example, Demo B — neither overrides it) | JSDoc | `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockWorkspace.spec.mjs`: the expiry call arrives once with `windowId: null` |
| the `expired` effect (`:788–790`) | this leaf | retained → no `onBindingReleased`; `afterTearOutWindowDisconnect({…, recovered: false, expired: true, pane: null})`; otherwise unchanged | as above | JSDoc on `bindNativeWindowSource` and `afterTearOutWindowDisconnect` | `DockWorkspace.spec.mjs`: a retaining host keeps its held pane alive past the lease and its hook sees `recovered: false`; the non-retaining control returns the item as today |
| `Workstation.view.Workspace#afterTearOutWindowDisconnect({recovered})` (`:2604–2614`) | #18309 — the documented contract | unchanged; its `recovered: false` branch gains its writer | — | none | the Workspace arm above |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A never-connected vessel whose host retains it keeps its live pane past the lease: at `reconnectLeaseMs` plus margin the same component instance is alive and unmounted — asserted on component identity (unit tier, PR #18635). Its second clause — a later re-tree resolving that instance from the cache without `createPane` — is a real-window effect on the flagship, deferred to #18621 item 4 (its headed rig; owner @neo-opus-vega) and listed as the PR's residual.
- [ ] The `expired` effect asks `onNativeWindowRelease` once, with `windowId: null` and `expired: true`; a host answering `false` keeps its pane and its hook receives `recovered: false`. Unit arms for both answers.
- [ ] `settleDockPane` is not called on the retained route. Mutation-verified: reverting the branch reds the identity assertion, not boot or fixture.
- [ ] Non-retaining hosts are unchanged: the existing never-connected reintegration path stays green.
- [ ] Post-merge: the #18621 headed rig (both close modes at the `popup` event) records no `settleDockPane` and reads a live pane at +32 s on the flagship.

## Out of Scope

- The `released` route (connected vessels) — already retention-aware.
- A window that dies without any disconnect being delivered (#18621 sighting 2, one run in four, a Playwright `page.close()` artifact as far as measured).
- Closing vessels when their root leaves (D#18445) and the `headless-dirty` interlock.
- Whether a never-adopted pane should stay in `paneHandles` after a committed terminal — `capturePane`'s handle-first design is the engine's, and the control shows the held handle is harmless on the release route.

## Avoided Traps

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Fix it in the Workstation's `afterTearOutWindowDisconnect` | The pane is already destroyed when the hook runs (stack order: settle → `onDockPaneReturn` → the hook). |
| Teach `reintegrateItem` about other documents | It is the single-document return flow by contract; the host's answer exists one layer up. |
| Remember the release route's answer for the expiry route | Nothing to remember: a never-bound reservation never releases, so `onRelease` never runs for it — measured with a recorder on the hook, silent for 32 s. |
| Read the destroy as "the vessel was never really opened" | `getPopupStates()` reports `committed: true` and the vessel document lists the item for the full 32 s; with #18622 the topology bar offers recovery for it — recovery that would rebuild the pane. |
